transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhou (Redwood SE), Liam Rosen (Novaretail CTO), Priya Singh (Head of ML Ops), Derek Ho (Eng Manager)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost breakdown UI. Questions about caching, quantization, and private deployments. Action items captured at end.

00:00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE for Redwood. With me is Ethan our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
00:00:10 Liam: Good, thanks. Real quick - we're mostly focused today on the Console visibility and how you show per-route cost. Priya will share numbers.
00:00:20 Priya: Yeah, we want to understand cost by route because some of our batch jobs are spiking costs and we need to attribute to teams.
00:00:30 Ethan: Great, we'll jump into the Console and show the usage analytics. We'll focus on per-route dashboards, token breakdown, and the cost model assumptions so you can map to your billing. A reminder, the demo data is anonymized.
00:00:45 Derek: Cool. Also curious about host options - Hosted vs Dedicated and data residency.

00:05:12 Ethan: (screen share) Here's the main usage overview - total tokens, requests, p95 latency. You can filter by model, route, or API key. The per-route dashboard shows requests/hour, avg tokens in/out, and also a cost estimate column driven by your pricing plan.
00:05:45 Priya: How accurate is that cost estimate? Is it based on sample billing or some general rate?
00:05:55 Maya: Good question. By default it uses Redwood hosted list rates, but when you link your billing contract we can map committed rates or Dedicated SKU prices. The UI also lets you toggle quantization, batching and caching assumptions to see the sensitivity.
00:06:30 Ethan: For example, toggle on KV/prefix caching and you'll see modeled token savings on repeat queries. We also show batching impact - this is a modeled throughput improvement and per-token cost reduction line.

00:10:02 Liam: On that caching point - we have frequent chat-like requests where the prompt shares a large system prompt. Does the Console account for prefix caching and KV cache hits?
00:10:15 Ethan: Yes, we have a prefix/KV cache model. The dashboard has a metric 'cache hit rate' by route. If you click into a route you can see sessions where the KV cache reduced tokens and the modeled cost savings. The model assumes your app uses the Redwood SDK or standard cache headers.
00:10:40 Priya: Our concern is accuracy - if the model overstates savings we'll be surprised. Can you run an on-prem benchmark?
00:10:51 Maya: Absolutely - Ethan will run a benchmark with your sample payloads. We'll produce an empirical cost per 1M tokens under both Hosted and Dedicated assumptions.

00:15:20 Ethan: (narrating) Here is a per-route drilldown - route name, recent sample traces, token histogram, latency percentiles, and a cost waterfall. The waterfall shows model compute, inferred batching efficiency, and cache savings. There's also a 'what-if' slider to simulate increasing batching window from 30ms to 150ms and watch latency/cost move.
00:15:52 Derek: That slider is helpful. For our customer facing features, p95 latency under 400ms is key. If increasing batching breaks that we can't use it.
00:16:05 Ethan: Yep - you can pin SLOs per route and get recommended batch sizes that meet the latency SLO while maximizing throughput. The optimizer also suggests quantization profiles (8-bit, 4-bit) and shows predicted token-level quality delta.

00:20:10 Priya: Where do you store logs and audit trails? We need audit logs, KMS, and SOC2.
00:20:22 Maya: We support SOC2, and we have customer-level audit logs in the Console. For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) you can use your own KMS and retention policies. For Hosted we integrate with customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest if required by contract. We'll send the security pack after this call.
00:20:45 Liam: Great. Also need to confirm data residency - some of our tenant data must stay in EU.
00:20:53 Maya: We can pin region routing and have EU-only hosting for those routes. In Dedicated and Private that is straightforward.

00:25:05 Ethan: Back to cost modeling - here's an example where two routes call the same model but one has a much larger system prompt. You can compare cost-per-call and cost-per-1000-requests. The Console also exposes token-level attribution so you can say 'this route costs X per 1k' and export to CSV or our billing API.
00:25:40 Priya: Can we annotate routes to teams? We want chargeback to org teams.
00:25:48 Ethan: Yes - tags on routes and API keys. Then the analytics pivot by tag/team. We also show trendline alerts if a route's spend changes >20% week over week.

00:30:12 Derek: On Dedicated - what's the commit, and how does autoscaling/bursting work? If we commit to a pool, can we burst to host?
00:30:25 Maya: Dedicated has committed GPU pools with configurable burst capacity to Hosted in case you need short spikes. Commit levels determine baseline throughput and discounted per-token rates. We'll include a pricing matrix in the follow-up.
00:30:50 Ethan: Also note our smart routing can route by policy - route small latency-sensitive calls to low-latency nodes and heavy batch jobs to throughput-optimized nodes. That appears in the route config UI.

00:35:00 Priya: About model variants - can we fallback to a cheaper quantized variant automatically?
00:35:10 Ethan: Yes, the Console supports rollouts and fallback policies. You can set the primary model and a fallback with compatibility checks. The dashboard will show quality regressions based on your eval sets.

00:40:05 Liam: This is helpful. For the benchmark you mentioned, can you run with our prompt mix (we'll share a manifest) and include mixing short inference (100 tokens) and long context (8k)?
00:40:18 Ethan: Yes - please share the sample payloads and expected QPS. We'll run a 24h run and share p50/p95/p99, tokens consumed, and modeled cost under Hosted and Dedicated pricing.

00:45:20 Maya: Next steps recap: I'll send pilot pricing and the security pack. Ethan will run benchmarks and share results. Priya will send route list and QPS. We'll schedule a follow-up security call with your infra team.

00:50:00 Priya: One more question - do you provide usage APIs so we can pull per-route metrics into our internal BI?
00:50:10 Ethan: Yes, we have a usage API and webhook integration for alerts. Also export to S3/BigQuery for longer-term analytics.

00:53:00 Derek: Sounds good. Thanks for the walkthrough.
00:53:10 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up on action items.
00:53:20 Liam: Appreciate it. Bye.

Action items (captured):
- Maya: Send SOC2/compliance pack and pricing matrix (due 2026-03-01)
- Ethan: Run 24h benchmark with provided payloads; share results (due 2026-03-08)
- Priya: Share per-route QPS and route tagging (due 2026-02-28)

References mentioned: security pack link (sent after call), pilot pricing deck (will be shared), benchmark template (Ethan to run).
